{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVAV-ec8AAAABWI9K3Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BmJKvzg_sWc0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BmJKv", "number": 18, "title": "Add optional iterative render–compare–revise refinement for image-guided 3D models", "body": "## Problem

The current image-guided modeling flow produces a Blender model and exports it without an automated visual feedback loop. In particular, a result may approximate the input silhouette using simple primitive shapes while differing substantially in body proportions, surface detail, and reference-specific features. The current "inspect the result" instruction is not an explicit comparison of model renders against the provided images.

## Expected outcome

Add **optional, bounded iterative refinement** to existing gen3d modeling, using the already approved input image or concept + required multi-view references:

1. Generate the initial 3D scene through Codex + the local Blender MCP bridge.
2. Render the scene from corresponding camera viewpoints (front, left side, back, three-quarter where applicable; use the available view for a single image).
3. Have Codex inspect the **reference images and rendered images together**, producing a structured, saved comparison: silhouette, proportions, part placement, missing/extra features, colors/materials; for humanoids also anatomy/face/limbs/pose where visible.
4. Convert concrete discrepancies into revision instructions and **modify the same Blender scene**, then re-render/re-evaluate.
5. Repeat until the comparison passes an explicitly defined stop criterion, an iteration limit is reached, or the user-requested human review interrupts progression.

A "pass" is a pragmatic AI visual judgment, **not** a guarantee of photorealism or measured geometric accuracy. Never report unmeasured quality improvements as proven.

Expose simple per-project settings for **enable refinement** and **maximum iteration count**, with default **Off** to preserve existing behavior. Avoid speculative extra controls unless needed to deliver the requested loop. Clearly explain that each iteration consumes Codex time/usage.

Keep all evaluation reports, comparison renders, instructions and intermediate outputs inspectable in Web UI and the **same shared HTTP/MCP project state**, including partial or failed runs. Do not replace the original approved reference images or silently skip viewpoints.

Use the existing Blender MCP bridge, local Codex subscription workflow and currently supported modeling modes (**scratch and MPFB-assisted humanoid**). Do not add a paid image/3D API, new cloud dependency, or replace the approved concept/multi-view pipeline.

Existing optional human review checkpoints must remain authoritative. In automatic mode, run bounded refinement before presenting the final 3D preview review; do not silently bypass a required approval. Preserve versions, original artifacts, retries/revisions, GLB/.blend export, image-upload workflows and modeling-mode constraints. Report errors and iteration-limit exhaustion explicitly and retain usable partial artifacts.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] A project can enable/disable refinement and choose a bounded maximum number of revision cycles; settings persist across server restart and are visible via Web UI/HTTP/MCP.
- [ ] Off mode preserves the current modeling and review behavior; existing projects remain compatible.
- [ ] Enabled mode performs initial model → reference-aligned renders → structured comparison → actionable revision of the **existing scene** → fresh renders and re-evaluation. Verify at least one actual iteration path; do not count repeated prompts without geometry changes as refinement.
- [ ] Both uploaded-image and base+multi-view workflows provide their original images to evaluation; absent/unobservable details are treated as uncertain instead of invented ground truth.
- [ ] Stop conditions (acceptable result, max cycles, inspection/modeling failure, usage limit and review checkpoint) are explicit, terminate without infinite retries and do not masquerade as successful quality improvement.
- [ ] In-progress iterations, per-view renders, reports, revision instructions and associated scene/model artifacts are preserved with clear provenance and can be inspected through the existing UI and MCP/history without overwriting older versions.
- [ ] Test both scratch and MPFB paths (MPFB only for humanoids); retain the configured human review checkpoints, reference consistency policies, and exports.
- [ ] Run `npm test` and `npm run check` plus focused test coverage for settings/persistence, iteration and stop branches, review gating, partial-failure recovery, shared state/history and backwards compatibility. Record actual results.
- [ ] Where authenticated Codex and Blender are available, run relevant live integration checks, provide render comparisons and distinguish these from synthetic/mock tests. If unavailable, explicitly document the limitation; do not claim real quality improvement without evidence.
- [ ] Update relevant user/developer documentation and explain the new setting, iteration limit, usage implications and limitations.

## Post-merge verification

None.

## Optional validation

- Human visual comparison of before/after models on a difficult realistic humanoid and a geometric object. Useful for assessing aesthetic benefit but **not** a mandatory pre-merge gate without a reproducible standard.
- Additional real Blender trials across different hardware or profiles when available.

## Context

- #3 Project vision
- #10 Multi-view concept references
- #12 Consistency inspection settings
- #16 MPFB-assisted humanoid modeling
- `src/runner.js` — task prompt, Blender execution and export
- Existing pipeline deliberately requires approved images as modeling inputs; refinement must not bypass this or invent substitute references.

Scope: implement the requested feedback/refinement loop with minimal changes to existing architecture. If an implementation-dependent decision is genuinely unresolved, surface it instead of silently changing requirements.
